facts.content: Patient reports a 3-day history of diarrhea as the chief complaint.
Patient has had watery, loose diarrhea for 3 days with approximately 5 to 6 stools per day and no blood.
facts.source_text: • Diarrhea watery, loose, ~5–6 stools/day; no blood

facts.content: Patient had several episodes of vomiting at the start of the illness, which have now resolved.
facts.source_text: • Initial vomiting x few episodes now resolved

facts.content: Patient reports reduced appetite and poor oral intake.
Patient feels dehydrated and weak.
Patient reports a possible low-grade fever early in the illness but currently feels relatively fine.
facts.source_text: • Possible low-grade fever early in illness; currently feels "kind of fine"

facts.content: Patient denies abdominal pain, headache, and myalgias.
Symptoms began spontaneously at home with no known food, contact, or other exposure triggers.
facts.source_text: • Onset spontaneous at home; no known food/contacts/exposure

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses a blue reliever inhaler as needed.
Patient has no known allergies.
Patient's father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer about 10 years ago.
facts.source_text: • FH: father HTN, died of bowel cancer ~10y ago

facts.content: Patient's mother has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient lives alone and works as a software engineer.
Patient has been off work for 3 days.
Patient drinks alcohol infrequently.
Patient is a non-smoker.
Acute gastroenteritis with 3 days of watery diarrhea and initial vomiting, considered likely self-limited.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute gastroenteritis — 3 days watery diarrhea, initial vomiting; likely self-limited

facts.content: Dehydration due to decreased intake and ongoing stool losses.
facts.source_text: 2. Dehydration — subjective decreased intake + ongoing stool losses

facts.content: Asthma is intermittent and managed with a blue inhaler as needed.
facts.source_text: 3. Asthma — intermittent, uses blue inhaler PRN

facts.content: For gastroenteritis, provide supportive care and encourage oral fluid intake.
facts.source_text: • Gastroenteritis: supportive care; encourage oral fluids

facts.content: Oral rehydration solution is recommended, with Diurelite suggested.
facts.source_text: • Gastroenteritis: supportive care; encourage oral fluids; ORS recommended (Diurelite suggested)

facts.content: Paracetamol as needed is recommended for fever or feeling unwell.
facts.source_text: • Symptomatic: paracetamol PRN for fever/feeling unwell

facts.content: Patient is advised to take time off work for the next 1 to 2 days.
facts.source_text: • Work: advise time off for next 1–2 days

facts.content: Patient may return to work when diarrhea has been absent for 24 to 48 hours.
To address dehydration, patient is advised to increase oral fluid intake.
Electrolyte replacement with Diurelite is to be considered for dehydration.
Patient should have a review if not improved within one week.
facts.source_text: • Follow-up: review if not improved within 1 week

facts.content: Patient is instructed to re-contact if symptoms persist or worsen.
facts.source_text: patient instructed to re-contact if persistent/worsening symptoms
